n8.starta-servern-och-las.n9: Shapes and baseline memory examples use Llama-3-8B (8192 tokens); the chat format is for Instruct. This server runs Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct with the same core shapes and layer count, but frequency-dependent RoPE scaling and support for 131072 tokens (128K). The flag limits this run to 8192. vLLM v0.11.0 is the documentation reference for the V1 examples, not GPU-tested here; see docs/REFERENCES.md.
n8.disaggregerad-prefill-och-decode.2: Prefill and decode have different bottlenecks: prefill is compute-bound (once the prompt is large enough), decode is memory-bound. Running both on the same GPUs lets a long prompt disturb everyone waiting for the next token — ITL spikes exactly when a new request arrives.
n8.disaggregerad-prefill-och-decode.3: Disaggregation splits them: some GPUs run prefill, others decode, and the KV cache is moved between them. This reduces direct prefill interference in the decode pool, but load, context length and transfers still affect ITL.
n8.disaggregerad-prefill-och-decode.4:
KV per request = T · 32 layers · 8 heads · 128
                 · 2 (K and V) · 2 bytes
T = 5,000        → 625 MiB
100 Gbit/s       → ~52 ms
n8.disaggregerad-prefill-och-decode.5: The transfer costs time and bandwidth. Fast links such as NVLink or RDMA can make the split useful under strict ITL requirements. In vLLM v0.11.0 this is experimental: --kv-transfer-config requires a suitable connector and separate instance configuration, not just a flag.
n8.disaggregerad-prefill-och-decode.6: What you gain and what you pay:
n8.disaggregerad-prefill-och-decode.19: The hand-over costs too: decode needs the relevant KV data in place. How transfer and computation overlap depends on the connector. A long context and a slow link can eat the gain.
n8.multi-lora-manga-modeller-pa.1: Multi-LoRA: many models on one GPU
n8.multi-lora-manga-modeller-pa.2: In the course’s row-vector convention a LoRA adapter has two small matrices per weight W [d_in, d_out]: A [d_in, r] and B [r, d_out], with rank r, typically 8–64. This makes x A B compatible. The base weights are frozen and shared by all adapters.
n8.multi-lora-manga-modeller-pa.3:
y = x W + (α/r) · x A B
Base 8B bf16       16 GB (shared)
Adapter r = 16     ~84 MB
32 adapters        ~2.7 GB
n8.multi-lora-manga-modeller-pa.4: vLLM serves many adapters against the same base model at once. Requests with different adapters land in the same batch and the kernels apply the right adapter per request — so one GPU can serve many customers who each have their own fine-tuned variant.
n8.multi-lora-manga-modeller-pa.5: The cost is extra work per token when adapters are mixed in one batch. LoRA can improve task quality and learn new facts or skills; results depend on data, rank and training. It is neither a guarantee of better quality nor a reliable factual database.
n8.multi-lora-manga-modeller-pa.7: Each request names its adapter in the model field (for example "code"). The server keeps only --max-loras adapters active at a time and loads more on demand.
n8.multi-lora-manga-modeller-pa.8: The LoRA update is added to the frozen weight without changing its shape. The adapter must match the base checkpoint and target modules; matching shapes alone do not make it portable between base models. It can be moved between machines and merged into its base model. The memory example assumes bf16 and all seven attention/MLP projections per layer.
